context_documents.body:
> Physical evidence update 2026-11-07: read the complete [upgrade report](../PHYSICAL_UPGRADE_REPORT.md) and the new physical studies in `data/physical_studies.jsonl`. Earlier source accounts below retain their publication scopes.

# 2026-27: Preacceleration, passive restraint and retrofit compression

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The interview describes a two-X44 intake at 2.5:1, passive carbon upper roller, roller-floor transmission described as 17:19, and a 3-inch steel drum driven by four X60s with powered hood rollers. A previously powered upper feed roller was made passive after jamming. Drum-region compression is reported as 3/8 inch and final roller compression as 1/2 inch.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly connects the stepped compression to fitting a replacement shooter in the existing robot, and the passive roller change to avoiding fuel being driven downward into jams. Collector repair access is deliberate because it receives impacts.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The important reference is the sequence of contacts, not simply four launcher motors. Upstream acceleration reduces the velocity increment demanded of the drum, while the passive restraint prevents one contact from injecting fuel into an already occupied region. More powered surfaces can therefore lower useful flow. A retrofit also fixes the available path length and elevation; its compression distribution cannot safely be transplanted without the same incoming velocity and support geometry. Separately, the agitation priority hierarchy means collector deployment and automatic shooting agitation are competing commands rather than independent subsystems.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure hopper-to-exit rate and current with the upper restraint passive versus driven, at several fill levels. Check worn fuel and simultaneous agitation. Preserve the source ratio order until driver/driven orientation is verified.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p9H80uFyuu8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p9H80uFyuu8)

context_documents.body:
# 2026-27: Retained interview snapshot; overview thumbnail only

Generated from `data/physical_studies.jsonl`; edit that authoritative record.

## Whole robot and packaging

The retained interview describes an intake, roller floor and replacement drum shooter constrained by the existing chassis. The newly inspected publisher thumbnail establishes the exterior hopper walls, top mesh and exposed upper roller area on the numbered robot. It cannot establish the internal feed geometry. The side reconstruction below therefore shows only a functional contact order from the interview, with all distances, bumper crossing and module/electronics locations marked unknown. This is an honest partial reconstruction rather than a measured robot layout.

## Piece flow

The intake sends fuel to a roller floor. Upstream contacts accelerate it toward a 3-inch steel drum with powered hood rollers. The upper restraint became passive after its powered form drove balls downward into jams. Reported compression differs between drum and final roller; those values describe the retrofit contact regions, not universal spacing recommendations.

## Annotated views

Editorial reconstruction. Not to scale; only explicit dimension labels are source dimensions. No CAD-derived measurements. Dashed envelopes are schematic and not clearance certification.

![physical-2026-27-top](../../images/physical/physical-2026-27-top.png)

![physical-2026-27-side](../../images/physical/physical-2026-27-side.png)

![physical-2026-27-transition](../../images/physical/physical-2026-27-transition.png)

## Intake drive, floor and agitation ownership

### Published construction

The retained interview reports two X44 intake motors at 2.5:1 and a floor transmission labeled 17:19.

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

### Editorial operating reconstruction

Acquire into the hopper, then use floor transport to supply the replacement shooter. Intake deployment and automatic shooting agitation compete in a command priority hierarchy.

### Engineering interpretation

A control system must decide which command owns deploy motion. Simultaneous desired actions cannot be assumed to occur independently just because they appear in different subsystem lists.

### Transfer and compatibility limits

Transfer the command-ownership requirement. Preserve ambiguous 17:19 notation until driver and driven are established; the thumbnail does not establish the transmission.

### Unknowns

Ratio direction, floor roller dimensions, sensor mapping and exact command priorities need original code/CAD confirmation.

### Proposed validation, not performed

First inspect the missing source interface or CAD; only then test the specific capture/transfer failure that could change the architecture. No hardware experiment was performed in this upgrade.

Figure `physical-27-overview`. [Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p9H80uFyuu8). Cannot establish drum material, ratios, internal roller contact, dimensions, or event version.

## Passive restraint and stepped-compression retrofit

### Published construction

The interview reports a passive carbon upper restraint, a four-X60 3-inch steel drum, powered hood rollers, 3/8-inch drum-region compression and 1/2-inch final compression.

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

### Editorial operating reconstruction

Preaccelerated fuel reaches the drum while the passive upper contact supports/restraints it without actively pushing it downward. Final roller contact increases the reported compression before exit.

### Engineering interpretation

The relevant transfer is a sequence that avoids driving fuel into an occupied region. Changing an active contact to passive alters both velocity and reaction force. A different incoming speed or path length can reverse the benefit of the same nominal compression.

### Transfer and compatibility limits

Use passive versus powered restraint as a design question. Do not fabricate the original cross-section or transplant compression without defining free diameter, compressed gap and support direction.

### Unknowns

No inspected internal detail or video frame supports the contact locations. Compression definition, fuel condition, measured rate and electrical headroom remain unresolved.

### Proposed validation, not performed

First inspect the missing source interface or CAD; only then test the specific capture/transfer failure that could change the architecture. No hardware experiment was performed in this upgrade.

source_reviews.title: Team RUSH Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.locator: Watch description and retained interview study
source_reviews.review_basis: Read publisher description and older dossier. Attempted captions separately
source_reviews.facts: Publisher identifies intake, indexing and Kraken Cannon. Older study describes preacceleration, powered hood, passive guide and flow sensing.
source_reviews.limitations: Fresh caption requests returned no readable payload. Detailed construction and revisions are carry-forward claims.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Team RUSH publicly announced its 2026 robot before Chelsea, with later interview metadata naming its Kraken Cannon shooter and indexing system. The retained mechanism study describes a three-wide drum fitted into the existing robot. Its engineering lesson is the interaction between the footprint already allocated to scoring and the degree of positive control needed to keep fuel moving. The old account attributes jams to a powered upper roller, which was subsequently made passive. That is a testable explanation for why removing an actuator could improve net output.
piece_flow: The older account places a powered collector below a passive upper guide, with additional tubes to retain control across the entry.
A powered floor with successive roller contacts feeds a compact preacceleration path.
The retained report describes a drum and powered hood contacts, with a beam break used to signal that discharge has finished.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A retrofit retains existing interfaces. The older technical account describes variable compression to fit within the available space and passive hopper motion linked to deployment. Analyze the changing contact gap rather than treating the retained frame as empty space. Fuel volume, wiring access and collector motion should be checked through the full travel before evaluating launcher output.

subsystems.name: Collector and transfer
subsystems.construction: Retained account describes a main roller, passive carbon upper contact and active roller floor.
subsystems.operation: Pull across the entry, guide fuel clear of the intake and present it at the next contact.
subsystems.team_rationale: The old account associates a powered-to-passive change with reducing jams.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare queue growth, slip and wedging as each contact is powered or free. Test after a full bin compresses fuel backward.
subsystems.interfaces: Hopper linkage, upper contact and intake stow all share the collector sweep.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Look for damage to the exposed roller and test removal without disturbing the floor.
subsystems.unknowns: Original configuration and exact guide location.

subsystems.name: Shooter and feedback
subsystems.construction: Prior dossier describes a three-wide drum path, adjustable hood and beam break.
subsystems.operation: Accelerate fuel progressively, then use flow feedback to decide when to leave the shot.
subsystems.team_rationale: Retained rationale emphasizes compact retrofit geometry and detecting emptying.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A clear beam can mean no fuel reaches the sensor. Validate timing with other signals or an independent inventory count.
subsystems.interfaces: Exit readiness couples drive heading, hood, drum speed and feeder state.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test partial obstruction and vibration-induced sensor misalignment.
subsystems.unknowns: Measured recovery, sustained shot rate and exact compression profile.

revisions: Team reveal gives the early event schedule but does not describe an exact as-revealed mechanism set.
Retained study describes a drum retrofit and a change from a powered upper roller to a passive guide. Exact dates remain open.
transferable_principles: Test a passive guide against powered contact where the main job is preventing escape or bridging.
Instrument full-hopper emptying and measure how often an empty signal arrives while fuel remains upstream.
Keep an impacted collector easy to replace without resetting the shooter path.
disconfirming_conditions: A passive upper guide can lose when a steep rise or worn fuel needs active opposing traction.
Beam-break silence can mean a blocked or starved transfer rather than an empty hopper.
A compact variable-compression path can become more sensitive to fuel wear and dimensional spread.
remaining_gaps: No complete fresh captions or published 2026 source code found in the reviewed public team repository listing. Original shooter layout, retrofit date, exact dimensions and competitive configuration remain unconfirmed.
recommended_images: Interview frames showing the passive upper contact, full feed cross-section and open versus stowed hopper, pending visual review.
